stem.text: Describe the functions of the internal membranes of the chloroplast in photosynthesis.

points.text: photosynthetic / named / primary / accessory, pigments to absorb light (energy) ;
ref. to, photosystems / antenna complex and reaction centre / light harvesting structures ;
photoactivation / electrons excited / emission of electrons ;
electrons move along electron transport chain ;
site of photolysis / location of oxygen-evolving complex ;
thylakoid space or lumen to, form proton gradient / have high concentration of protons ;
thylakoid membrane is (relatively) impermeable, to maintain the proton gradient ;

explanation.text: Separate the membrane surface from the space it encloses. The membrane houses pigments, carriers and ATP synthase; its low proton permeability helps the thylakoid lumen maintain a different proton concentration from the stroma.

reasoningChain: Locate the light-absorbing and electron-transfer components.
Connect proton return through ATP synthase with ATP formation.

stem.text: Rubisco activase (RA) is an enzyme that has an effect on the activity of rubisco.
An investigation was carried out on the effect of RA on the activity of rubisco.

items: Solutions of rubisco and RuBP were added to two tubes, A and B.
Both tubes were incubated at 25 °C for 6 minutes.
The activity of rubisco was measured every 30 seconds.

stem.text: All conditions were kept the same, except for the addition of RA to tube A.
The results are shown in Fig. 8.1.

stem.caption: Fig. 8.1
stem.alt: Rubisco activity over six minutes in tube A with rubisco activase and tube B without rubisco activase.

stem.text: Describe the results shown in Fig. 8.1 and suggest an explanation for the effect of RA on the activity of rubisco.

points.text: A activity increases and B activity remains, low / constant ;

comparative data quote ;
e.g. 3.0–3.2 at 0.5 mins and 11.4–11.6 at 6 mins for A
0.4 throughout for B
by changing the active site of rubisco ;

by enabling rubisco to bind more readily with, RuBP / substrate
or
more enzyme–substrate complexes ;
enables products to leave active site more quickly ;

explanation.text: Because the tubes differ only in RA, the comparison isolates the effect of adding RA under the stated conditions. A description of the activity curves and a proposed molecular explanation answer different parts of the instruction.

reasoningChain: Compare the two curves with numerical evidence.
Link the treatment difference to rubisco activity.
Explain how active-site availability can change enzyme–substrate complex formation.

bullets: Many responses demonstrated a very good knowledge and understanding of the functions of the internal membranes of a chloroplast.

Most candidates correctly described the results and recognised that the effect of adding rubisco activase was to increase the activity of rubisco. Most attempted to support this observation by quoting data from the graph but many did not read off values with sufficient care and stated inaccurate figures as a consequence.

Explanations of the results often noted that rubisco activase activates rubisco by enabling the substrate to bind to the enzyme. However, very few elaborated this further by considering conformational changes to the active site or changes to the activation energy.
